theme: Airline fare tracking datasets (Google Flights scrapers, Skyscanner, Hopper reports), airfare price indices
queries_run: gh search repos "google flights scraper" --sort stars
gh search repos "airfare price dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "flight price dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "BTS airfare" OR "DB1B" --sort stars

candidates.name: AWeirdDev/flights
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library (MIT, 2047 stars, updated 14 Sep 2026 - actively maintained) that queries Google Flights' internal protobuf API for live one-way/round-trip fares, no key needed. No committed price panel itself, but is a working, current, high-quality one-command pull method for building a route-level airfare time series from scratch.
candidates.why_useful: Airfare levels are a travel-demand/consumer-discretionary proxy that reads on ABNB nights and ADR (kernel analogue per gap list). Fastest available method to start a point-in-time airfare pull; would need daily cron to become a vintage series (gap 4).

candidates.name: ScrapingBee/google-flights-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/Node client wrapping ScrapingBee's proxy service to extract Google Flights fares, routes, schedules with JS rendering. Commercial-API-gated, no data committed.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative acquisition method for airfare nowcasting; requires a paid ScrapingBee key so lower priority than AWeirdDev/flights.

candidates.name: derekcheungsa/flight-monitor
candidates.what_it_holds: Flight price monitor app: Google Flights scraper plus dashboard, date scanning, and price-history storage (implies it accumulates a local time series, likely SQLite/CSV, though no long-run export confirmed from README alone).
candidates.why_useful: If run continuously this produces exactly the kind of route-level fare time series useful as a travel-demand proxy; worth a closer look at whether historical exports exist.

candidates.name: ropensci/skynet
candidates.what_it_holds: rOpenSci-reviewed R package that downloads and builds passenger/traffic networks directly from US DOT BTS DB1B (fare/itinerary survey) and T-100 (segment traffic) data; includes functions to pull, clean, and network-ize official government airline fare and capacity data going back decades.
candidates.why_useful: DB1B/T-100 are the exact 'airline capacity and traffic' data named in gap 10; this is a maintained, peer-reviewed one-command pull method for a large, free, official US domestic fare/traffic dataset spanning 1990s-present, directly usable as a travel-volume/pricing proxy.
candidates.time_coverage: BTS DB1B/T-100 back to early 1990s, quarterly
candidates.size_hint: package code; underlying BTS source files are multi-GB per quarter

candidates.name: i-baumann/DB1B_Automation
candidates.what_it_holds: Automation scripts to download and process BTS DB1B fare survey files programmatically (MIT licence, updated Oct 2025).
candidates.why_useful: Lowers the cost of building a US domestic airfare/traffic panel from the official DOT source named in gap 10.

candidates.name: clementhennet/DB1B_data_extraction
candidates.what_it_holds: 'DB1B Data Downloader: U.S. Airline Market Analysis' - a puller for BTS DB1B market/fare files, updated May 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Another maintained DB1B extraction tool; redundant with skynet/DB1B_Automation but confirms the data is easily pullable for an airfare-level proxy.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps with ropensci/skynet and i-baumann/DB1B_Automation as an acquisition method for the same BTS source

candidates.name: Trevorkaaya21/airline-market-power-analysis-
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis of US domestic DB1B fares computing HHI (market concentration), price dispersion, and demand elasticity by route with pandas; likely includes a processed fare table derived from DB1B, updated Dec 2025.
candidates.why_useful: Could be a source of ready-processed route-level fare/elasticity output rather than raw DB1B, saving reprocessing time if it holds committed CSVs.

candidates.name: zlacet/DOT-DB1B-Analytics-Pipeline
candidates.what_it_holds: End-to-end pipeline: DOT DB1B fare data -> Python ETL -> PostgreSQL -> Tableau dashboard with automated reporting, updated Sep 2026 (MIT).
candidates.why_useful: A recent, full ETL reference implementation for turning raw DB1B fare files into an analyzable warehouse; useful as a build template even without a stored dataset.
candidates.size_hint: pipeline code, no data committed (DB warehouse)

candidates.name: steveriffe/AvDB
candidates.what_it_holds: 'Exploratory Analytics & Visualizations of DB1B and BTS data', updated 7 Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Another active DB1B/BTS analysis repo; worth checking for committed processed extracts.

candidates.name: Elvi3n/Fabric-Medallion-Pipeline-Airline-Origin-and-Destination-Survey-DB1B
candidates.what_it_holds: Microsoft Fabric / PySpark medallion-architecture pipeline built on BTS DB1B origin-and-destination survey data, updated Apr 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Another engineering template for ingesting DB1B; marginal beyond the other DB1B tools already listed.

candidates.name: saragadam-rohith/airfare-index
candidates.what_it_holds: Interactive Streamlit/Plotly app that processes airfare data and computes/visualizes a price index across routes, airlines, time periods; updated Aug 2026. Part of a large cluster of near-identical 'Smart India Hackathon 2026 SIH26056' student teams (dozens of repos named airfare-index / apix-airfare-index / mospi-airfare-index) building a real-time Indian domestic airfare CPI-style index via web scraping of OTAs, for India's MoSPI/NSO.
candidates.why_useful: If any of these SIH26056 teams committed working scraper+index code and sample output, it is a template for a India-domestic airfare price index (Jevons-index CPI methodology) that could proxy APAC/India travel-cost inflation (gap 7 APAC regional). Quality/completeness is unverified across ~25 near-duplicate student repos found; flagging the cluster rather than each repo.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: cluster of ~25 near-identical hackathon submissions (e.g. chakradharreddy141-netizen/airfare-index, dspro2345-cpu/mospi-airfare-index, TushKum/apix-airfare-index, rishabhdeepak/airfare-indexer) all targeting the same India MoSPI SIH26056 problem statement; only listing one representative

candidates.name: rishabhnair12345/skyscanner_scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python flight-price tracker using the Skyscanner (RapidAPI) endpoint to fetch cheapest fares between two airports; updated May 2025.
candidates.why_useful: Small but working Skyscanner-based acquisition method; requires a RapidAPI key, no stored history.

candidates.name: romankh3/flights-monitoring
candidates.what_it_holds: Application for monitoring flight cost based on the Skyscanner API, deployed on Heroku with a Swagger-documented REST API; Apache-2.0, updated Dec 2025.
candidates.why_useful: A deployable monitoring service rather than a dataset; would need to be run over time to build a fare series.

candidates.name: naiborhujosua/Flight-Price-Prediction
candidates.what_it_holds: Uses the well-known Kaggle 'Flight Price Dataset' (India domestic fares, ~10K-300K rows depending on version) for airfare prediction modeling.
candidates.why_useful: Same static Kaggle flight-fare dataset re-used across dozens of near-identical EDA/ML repos found in this search (Flight-Price-EDA, Feature-Engineering-on-Flight-Price-Dataset, etc.); flagged once as a pointer since the underlying Kaggle set could theoretically serve as a historical India-airfare cross-section, but it is static, non-refreshing, and already the kind of single-well-known-dataset re-analysis the brief says to exclude.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same Kaggle Flight Price Dataset re-analyzed in ~30 near-identical repos surfaced by this search (excluded individually per brief's exclusion rule)
candidates.size_hint: single Kaggle CSV, exact row count unconfirmed

notes: Used all 6 permitted gh search calls (google flights scraper, airfare price dataset [0 hits], flight price dataset, airfare index/hopper, skyscanner api, BTS DB1B). No rate-limit errors hit. The 'airfare price dataset' and 'hopper flight price' queries both returned zero repos -- no GitHub-hosted equivalent of Hopper's fare-prediction reports or a maintained historical airfare price-index dataset was found; the space is dominated by (a) live-scrape tools with no stored history (Google Flights / Skyscanner API clients) and (b) a large cluster of near-duplicate Indian SIH-2026 hackathon student projects building a real-time domestic airfare CPI index for MoSPI, none of which appear to have committed usable multi-period data yet. The most substantive lead for ABNB purposes is not airline-fare-specific at all: BTS DB1B/T-100 airline traffic and fare survey data (US DOT, official, decades of history) is well covered by maintained open-source pullers (ropensci/skynet is the strongest, rOpenSci-reviewed). No committed, ready-to-use historical airfare price panel (multi-year, multi-route, with dates) was found anywhere in this search; everything usable is either a live-query method or points to the single static Kaggle India flight-price CSV already well-trodden by ML tutorials. Recommend a future scout specifically target 'IATA AirfareWatchdog', 'Cirium', or academic replication packages for airfare indices (BLS CPI airfares is already held per CONTEXT.md) rather than more GitHub scraper repos of this type.
